analysis: The PR changes only documentation: docs/architecture/inference.md (date bump at line 3 plus a new paragraph at head lines 1960-1973 on a Qwen JSON response_format thinking default) and docs/developer/test.md (date bump plus a paragraph at about lines 920-926 on prompt-contract vector regeneration). No source, key handling, attestation, authorization, encryption, cache-storage or wire-protocol code changed, so no TB-002, TB-003, TB-007 or TB-011 control is weakened. The supplied inference.md units (head lines 2045-2852) are unchanged surrounding context. They describe existing behavior and were reviewed for incidental security-relevant claims. Those claims keep fail-closed behavior: refusals log closed reason codes without request text (invariant 10), encrypted-prefix-cache posture matches T-041, and GLM tool-suffix validation fails closed. The new Qwen JSON response_format thinking default alters the rendered prompt. The docs say the coordinator prompt sidecar mirrors the rule, so cache planning renders the same prompt. This is a platform-owned contract that the supplied evidence cannot verify. If the prompt-contract identity or cache salt were not updated, cache-planning drift could result. That is a correctness and routing concern, not a demonstrated security regression, and the docs require regenerated vectors plus scripts/verify-prompt-parity.sh. The test.md addition, that vectors are copied byte-for-byte with a recorded source revision and SHA-256, strengthens provenance. Residual question: the actual provider code change and the platform sidecar change are not in this batch, so the Qwen35TemplateFix.applies predicate and Qwen4SupportPolicy.validateReasoningContext behavior could not be inspected. No threat-model update is needed from this docs-only change.
